beats.text: Life satisfaction falls until your late forties. Then it climbs back.
Four thousand Scottish adults rated their life from zero to ten.
Eight point one in your early twenties. Seven point five around fifty.
Then back up to seven point nine in your late sixties.
In a hundred and thirty-two countries, the low point is around forty-eight.
The dip is small, but real. If midlife feels heavy, you're right on schedule.

sources: Scottish Health Survey 2016, Volume 1, Table 8.7 (life satisfaction mean scores by age, all adults, 0–10): 16–24 8.1, 25–34 7.9, 35–44 7.7, 45–54 7.5, 55–64 7.6, 65–74 7.9, 75+ 7.8; n = 4,309 (unweighted).

Blanchflower (2021), Is happiness U-shaped everywhere? Age and subjective well-being in 145 countries, Journal of Population Economics 34, 575–624 (NBER WP 26641: 132 countries) – U-shape minimum at age 47.2 (advanced countries) and 48.2 (developing countries).
Caveat: cross-sectional data; some longitudinal studies find a weaker or no U (e.g. Galambos et al. 2020). EU-SILC 2013 (Eurostat) shows decline into old age without a clear rebound at 75+.
